readme.html:
Open-source Rust coding agent for your terminal. Any model, multi-agent fleets, OS sandboxing, and verifiable receipts.

curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | sh

Install

The install script above puts checksum-verified codewhale and its short alias codew in ~/.local/bin on macOS and Linux. If your shell reports command not found, add ~/.local/bin to your PATH (details). Upgrade in place with codewhale update.

winget install --id HunterBown.CodeWhale --exact --source winget  # Windows x64
npm install -g codewhale                                          # wraps the same release binaries
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked                              # builds from source; can trail GitHub Releases

Prebuilt binaries ship for Linux, macOS, and Windows (x64 and arm64). Scoop, Nix, Homebrew on Linux, Android/Termux (preview), and manual downloads are in docs/INSTALL.md; container images are in docs/DOCKER.md. Use one install method per machine so two binaries do not shadow each other on PATH.

Quickstart

  1. Commit or stash your work, then run codewhale from a git repository root.
  2. Run /provider (or press F3) to select a provider, paste an API key, and pick a model. DeepSeek is the default; if no key is configured and a local Ollama server responds, Codewhale offers its models on your first message.
  3. Give it a task:
Fix the failing tests and explain what changed.

Read-only commands run immediately. Mutating shell commands prompt for approval: y runs once, a allows matching commands for the rest of the session, and n denies. Run /undo to revert the last turn and its file edits, or /help for commands and keybindings.

Capabilities

  • 50+ built-in providers and local models: Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek (deepseek-flash / V4.1 Flash by default; details), Google, Mistral, Moonshot, OpenRouter, xAI, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and local runtimes via Ollama, vLLM, or SGLang. Switch models mid-session with /model, route per-turn with /model auto (/router), and inspect latency and cost with /turn inspect. See Providers.
  • Receipts and rollback: /receipts (or codewhale receipts --last after exiting) records changed files, commands, web/MCP calls, sub-agents, approvals, and failures. /undo reverts the last turn in one step; /restore rolls the workspace back to an earlier snapshot (requires /trust on or Full Access). See Receipts.
  • Sub-agents, Fleets, and workflows: Carry multi-turn objectives with /goal, delegate work to sub-agents, coordinate role- and model-specific Fleets, or run repository-checked workflows.
  • MCP, skills, hooks, and plugins: Attach MCP servers, skills, plugins, and lifecycle hooks. Experimental code mode (execute_tools) batches multiple MCP/plugin calls under your normal approval rules. Optional macOS Computer Use stays off until explicitly reviewed and enabled.
  • Drop-in compatibility: Reads AGENTS.md automatically. Opt into CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, or .github/copilot-instructions.md via project_instruction_imports in config.example.toml. Import Claude Code settings and MCP servers with /import-claude, or install Claude Code plugins (skills, commands, agent profiles, MCP) and DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugins with /plugin install (details).

Entry points

Command Purpose
codewhale Interactive terminal app
codewhale exec "…" Headless single-task runner for scripts and CI (guide; --auto uses Full Access unless sandboxed)
codewhale web Local web client on 127.0.0.1 (guide)
codewhale review --pr N Advisory GitHub PR review; GitHub bot setup runs it on your own key
codewhale app-server --http Local HTTP Runtime API for threads, events, approvals, and per-turn diffs
codewhale serve --acp Agent Client Protocol over stdio for editors such as Zed

All entry points share one Rust engine (architecture). A community-maintained VS Code extension (source) connects to the same engine. See the latest release notes and roadmap for current release and desktop/cloud status.

Permissions, sandboxing, and privacy

Shift+Tab cycles permission modes: Ask → Accept Edits → Plan → Auto-Review → Full Access (Tab only completes). Accept Edits (default) applies edits inside the git repository and asks before commands. Ask prompts on every edit and command. Plan is read-only. Auto-Review uses rules and a reviewer model to approve routine calls and block high-risk ones. Full Access skips prompts and disables the OS sandbox (repository rules and managed policy still apply). See Modes.

In Ask, Accept Edits, and Auto-Review, commands run inside an OS sandbox where available: Seatbelt on macOS and bubblewrap on Linux (Windows has no OS sandbox yet). Sandboxed commands and terminal sessions cannot read credential paths such as ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or .env files. Run /preview-request to inspect a redacted outgoing request before sending it.

API keys added with /provider stay on your machine, and local models require no key. /cost and the footer track session spend when pricing is known (an unknown price is shown as unknown, never as free).

Aggregate telemetry is enabled by default (version, OS, session length/outcome, built-in provider IDs, bundled public-catalog model IDs (custom, private, or local models map to other), aggregate token totals, built-in tool call/error counts, and feature/error counters; rotating 90-day random install ID; never code, prompts, conversations, custom/private model names, file/repo/branch names, credentials, or IP addresses). Disable it with:

codewhale config set telemetry false

At startup Codewhale also checks GitHub for a new release (CODEWHALE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 to skip) and refreshes the public models.dev model catalog every 24 hours (CODEWHALE_DISABLE_MODELS_DEV_FETCH=1 or [catalog] auto_refresh = false to skip; suppressed automatically in CI and under DO_NOT_TRACK). Details: authorization order, sandboxing, and telemetry.

Contributing and license

The contributor wall (scripts/contributor-wall.py) tracks code, co-authored commits, carried-forward PRs, and credited reports. Bug reports and feature proposals go to Issues, questions to Discussions, and PR guidelines plus layout are in CONTRIBUTING.md (project structure). Join us on Discord or add hunterbown on WeChat for the Whale Brothers group.

Codewhale started as deepseek-tui and remains backward-compatible with its config and sessions. It is independently maintained and not affiliated with DeepSeek or any other model provider.

MIT. Third-party notices: vendored sources and adapted designs.

skills.name: agent-experience
skills.description: Use when writing or changing a model-facing tool definition (name, description, parameter schema, or its system-prompt section), and when designing skills, context loading, or multi-step workflows, to make information discoverable and use context efficiently.

skills.name: cordis-composition-reference
skills.description: Use when writing or reading a Cordis bundle patch or agent preset for this harness and you need the Loader YAML dialect (insert, override by id, group, disabled, isolate, !!js) or the list of installable Harness plugin packages and what each provides.

skills.name: cordis-plugin-development
skills.description: Use when designing, reviewing, adding, enabling, disabling, installing, configuring, or debugging a plugin, bundle, feature, page, panel, tool, or MCP connection in the current Harness profile, including a shipped plugin that is disabled by default, and for any visual object, decoration, or widget r

skills.name: editing-cordis-compositions
skills.description: Use when creating, changing, or validating an agent preset or other Cordis composition for this harness, including deciding host versus preset placement and checking that an authored preset mounts.

skills.name: batch
skills.description: Break a large, parallelizable goal into bounded work units, coordinate existing agent/worktree machinery, integrate, and verify. Explicit-only.

skills.name: best-of-n
skills.description: Generate a small set of independent candidate solutions in worktrees, judge them against one explicit rubric, and apply the winner only after PASS verification.

skills.name: contributor-onboarding
skills.description: Help a new contributor get productive on this checkout - inspect sync state against main, build, run the repository's exact verification gate, and produce a local what's-new digest. Never fetches, pulls, or modifies a dirty tree on its own. Explicit-only.

skills.name: dataviz
skills.description: Choose and produce an appropriate chart/dashboard/visual explanation from data, with legible encodings and source/assumption notes.

skills.name: debug
skills.description: Reproduce, minimize, localize, identify root cause, and distinguish diagnosis from an authorized fix. Prefer root-cause over symptom patches.

skills.name: delegate
skills.description: Strategic delegation for multi-step coding, research, or verification work. Use when a task can be split into parent reasoning plus focused sub-agent execution through the agent tool.

skills.name: dependency-update
skills.description: Read release notes/changelogs, update a defined dependency scope, handle breaking changes, and verify. Explicit-only; no broad update-everything by inference.

skills.name: document
skills.description: Write or update repository/product documentation: README, user guides, API docs, architecture, migration notes, and changelog material. This is not the Word-document artifact skill.

skills.name: documents
skills.description: Compatibility alias for the docx skill. Prefer loading docx.

skills.name: docx
skills.description: Create/edit/inspect Word documents using available managed or host capabilities.

skills.name: feedback

skills.name: feishu
skills.description: Work with Feishu or Lark bots, docs, sheets, bitables, approval flows, and OpenAPI/MCP setup without hardcoding credentials.

skills.name: fleet-manager
skills.description: Use when managing, triaging, restarting, escalating, or summarizing Codewhale fleet runs and workers.

skills.name: flights
skills.description: Track flights and look up status and schedules. Use when: flight status, track a flight, flightaware, arrivals, departures, delays, or a flight number.

skills.name: forget
skills.description: Help the user remove a stored fact using Codewhale's Context Lens when they ask to forget or delete a memory.

skills.name: frontend-design
skills.description: Produce intentional, responsive, accessible UI work and perform visual QA instead of generic component assembly.

skills.name: github
skills.description: GitHub via gh — issues, PRs, reviews, search, and CI runs. Use when: user mentions a repo, issue, PR, review, release, workflow run, or anything on github.com.

skills.name: gmail
skills.description: Search, read, draft, and send Gmail when the user asks to work with their inbox or email.

skills.name: google-calendar
skills.description: Read schedules, check availability, and create or update Google Calendar events when the user asks to work with their calendar.

skills.name: handoff

skills.name: implement

skills.name: interview

skills.name: mcp-discovery

skills.name: money

skills.name: pdf

skills.name: personal-goals

skills.name: photos

skills.name: plan

skills.name: plugin-creator

skills.name: podcast

skills.name: presentations
